## Summary

Per-seat pricing charges a recurring fixed amount per unit. The customer selects the number of seats and the merchant creates the Subscription with the recurring Price and seat count as the item’s `quantity`. Each unit represents a user or license.

## Key API Difference from Flat Rate

```js
stripe.subscriptions.create({
  customer: id,
  items: [{ price: per_seat_price_id, quantity: 12 }]  // ← quantity = number of seats
})
```

## Dashboard Start and Scheduling

Both captures illustrate creating a Product and recurring monthly Price, then selecting the customer and Price under **Billing → Subscriptions**. The Product description and Stripe Tax collection are optional in the illustrated flow.

- **May 12, 2026**: **Start subscription** starts immediately. For a scheduled start, switch to the classic editor and select **Schedule subscription**.
- **November 7, 2026**: **Start subscription** and **Schedule subscription** appear as alternative actions in the instructions. This guide omits the May classic-editor step. That difference leaves classic-editor availability and account rollout unresolved.

> [!note] Catalog editing in the dated guides
> Both per-seat walkthroughs say to edit the illustrated Product and Price before creating a Subscription with them. The November Products and Prices management guide allows later edits to permitted attributes and recommends a replacement Price for a new amount. An existing Price’s amount cannot be edited via the API. See [[source-stripe-products-prices]].

subscriptions-pricing-models-per-seat-pr.text: Per-seat pricing is a linear pricing model where the number of seats (for example, software licenses) maps to the number of units (for example, users).
Click **Start subscription** to start it immediately or **Schedule subscription** to start it on another schedule.
When you create the [subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions.md), specify a `quantity` to charge for the number of seats.
You can only edit the product and price until you create a subscription with them.
To schedule a subscription, switch to the classic editor, and click **Schedule subscription**.
You can only edit the product and price until you create a subscription with them.
